card: This pull request expands the util::Result template class to support structured failure types, multiple error and warning messages, and an update method to merge sequential results. Previously, util::Result was restricted to single bilingual error strings without structured failure data, preventing its use in functions like LoadChainstate that require callers to distinguish between fatal and recoverable error conditions. It demonstrates the utility by converting chainstate loading and verification routines from ad-hoc tuples to util::Result and shrinks the memory footprint of util::Result by heap-allocating failure states. Open PRs #25722 and #29700 build on this to standardize wallet loading and kernel error reporting.
changed_since_previous: Added workarounds in win64 and native_previous_releases CI scripts for GCC -Wmaybe-uninitialized false positives triggered by Result member access, and fixed a clang-tidy performance-no-automatic-move warning in wallet code.
evidence: PR description: 'This is a key missing feature that makes the result class not useful for functions like LoadChainstate() which produce different errors that need to be handled differently.'
PR description: 'Followup PRs #25722 and #29700 use it more broadly to return errors and warnings from wallet and kernel functions as well.'
problem: util::Result previously could only return a success value or a single bilingual error string. Functions that need structured failure codes to differentiate error types—such as distinguishing recoverable chainstate corruption requiring a reindex from unrecoverable fatal errors—or functions returning multiple warnings and errors had to rely on out-parameters and ad-hoc tuples.

risk.why: A mistake in chainstate load error propagation or interruption handling could cause node initialization to misclassify fatal errors or fail to trigger recovery prompts like reindexing.

scope_notes: The diff includes template metaprogramming in util/result.h and updates CMake files to add the new util/messages.cpp to bitcoin_util and bitcoinkernel libraries, alongside CI configuration workarounds for GCC maybe-uninitialized false positives.
summary: Expands util::Result to support typed failure values, multiple error and warning messages, and an update method to merge result states while preserving messages. The memory footprint of util::Result is reduced by heap-allocating failure objects. Chainstate loading and verification in init and node/chainstate are converted from custom status tuples to the updated util::Result interface.
